A Formalization of PA Unprovability of the Laver Function's Totality

The PKU AI4Math team has formalized in Lean Renrui Qi's proof that, under the I3 axiom, the Laver function $F(n)$ grows faster than fε0(n)f_{\varepsilon_0}(n)fε0​​(n) — hence its totality is unprovable in Peano Arithmetic (PA). This is a cross-domain result resolves a problem in mathematical logic open since 1993. The proof draws heavily on googology, a branch of recreational mathematics dedicated to the study of large numbers. Because the proof mixes mathematical logic with googology techniques unfamiliar to most reviewers, conventional peer review is hard; formalization offers a credible independent verification path.

@Zhiyuan Zhang completed the entire formalization, in a process with intensive human–AI collaboration throughout: the AI expanded and paraphrased the proof, carried out the main formalization work, and jointly discussed subtle mathematical points with the human, who steered the formalization direction in turn.

The formalization is sorry-free and passes the comparator's check. Beyond verification, we found and fixed several minor issues (none affecting the main strategy), compiled them into a report sent to Qi, and Qi incorporated our corrections into arXiv v5. The repo (with report) is at https://github.com/frenzymath/lavertable/.

For the full story — the background, our approach, and how formalization helped — see our blog post: https://frenzymath.com/blog/lavertable/.

Fun note: we also formalized Qi's Laver table yarn (LTY) notation in the same paper — according to Qi, possibly the strongest recursive ordinal notation ever to have appeared in mathematical history (apart from the kind that cheats using provability).
